label: rem:q-from-epsilon-rationale
title: Primitivity of $\varepsilon$ and the $q-1 \leftrightarrow \varepsilon$ convention
html:
Consistency with the q-parametrisation. The Frobenius--Hopf substrate A_q is recovered as the evaluation of the \varepsilon-expansion A_q = A_1 + \varepsilon \, \phi_1 + \varepsilon^2 \, \phi_2 + \cdots. Nothing in the algebraic q-theory changes: every identity in q - 1 rewrites directly in terms of \varepsilon, and the classical point \varepsilon = 0 coincides with q = 1.

Motivation for taking \varepsilon as primitive. First, categorical origin. The Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon is intrinsic to A before any braiding is chosen. Second, exact error bounds. With \varepsilon primitive and living in an ordered field with infinitesimals, the scaling laws become literal arithmetic inequalities.
